\caption{State-level projections of cervical cancer incidence and mortality in 2050 under a single-round screening programme at 70\% coverage with HPV DNA testing, VIA or Pap cytology, by region. Observed rates are the 2012--19 means of the population-based cancer registry estimates used for calibration (ICMR-NINE). Screening starts in 2026 and reaches 70\% of women aged 30--65 years. The tests differ in the model only in their sensitivity for high-risk HPV infection ($H^+$): Pap cytology 0.70, visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) 0.75, liquid-based cytology (LBC) 0.85 and HPV DNA testing 0.95. Rates are per 100{,}000 women; values are means of 1000 stochastic simulations with 95\% intervals. Reductions are relative to no screening in the same year. First year CIR $<$ 4 is the first calendar year in which the mean CIR falls below 4 per 100{,}000 (the proxy for the WHO elimination threshold used in this study; -- = not reached by 2070). States are ordered within region by projected no-screening CIR in 2026. HPV DNA testing at 2040 and 2060, and liquid-based cytology, are reported in the Supplementary Material (Appendix~K, Tables S10 and S11). India row: dedicated national model; state rows: independently calibrated state models. CIR=crude incidence rate. CMR=crude mortality rate.}
\label{tab:state_policy}
